source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: Primary paper re-read. Voyager (curriculum + skill library + iterative prompting with self-verification) beats ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT on exploration and the tech tree. Skills are only added after self-verification says the task succeeded.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 prompting iterations (3.3x the baselines). Tech tree, 3 runs each, mean iterations: AutoGPT wood 92, stone 94, iron 135, diamond 0/3. Voyager wood 6, stone 11, iron 21, diamond 1/3 (102 iterations). ReAct and Reflexion 0/3 at every level. Voyager without skill library: wood 7, stone 9, iron 29, diamond 0/3.
quote: Voyager w/o skill library exhibits a tendency to plateau in the later stages.
limits: 3 runs per method. GPT-4 only. Minecraft, not reasoning. The library effect on early tiers is small or negative (stone 11 vs 9 iterations); it shows up at iron and diamond.
agent_relevance: Closes gap 7 on the numbers: the library gain is real but concentrated in later, compositional tasks, so early-stage gain should not be expected.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager, ablation section 3.4 and appendix retrieval accuracy
finding: Ablations separate verification from the library. Removing self-verification cost more items than removing the library. The library mattered for later plateau and for transfer. Skill retrieval used top-5 skills per query and was measured.
numbers: Random curriculum: -93% discovered items. No self-verification: -73% items (the most important feedback type). GPT-3.5 instead of GPT-4: 5.7x fewer items. Retrieval top-5 accuracy 96.5% (appendix Table A.4). Ablation values are read from text; the figure bars were not extracted.
quote: Self-verification is the most important among all the feedback types.
limits: Verification here is used both to gate library additions and to decide when to move on or retry, so the effect is not purely a gate effect. The paper has no run of library filled after every attempt versus library filled only after verified success.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gaps 1 and 7: verification is the larger lever than the library in Voyager, but its effect is confounded with task retry control. The trigger-versus-gate split is still untested.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager, Table 2 zero-shot generalisation
finding: A library built by Voyager in one world, reused in a new world on four unseen tasks, cuts iterations and lets AutoGPT solve some tasks it otherwise fails.
numbers: Iterations to solve (3 trials): Voyager with library 19/18/21/18 (diamond pickaxe, golden sword, lava bucket, compass), 3/3 each. Voyager without library 36 (2/3), 30 (3/3), 27 (3/3), 26 (3/3). AutoGPT 0/3 on all four; AutoGPT with Voyager's library 39 (1/3), 30 (1/3), 0/3, 30 (2/3). Cap 50 iterations.
limits: Four tasks, three trials, a library that was built for exactly this game, so reuse is in-domain. No measure of wrong reuse.
agent_relevance: Shows a verified library is portable across agents and cuts steps roughly 30-50%; says nothing about false reuse.

source: Soar Manual, chapter 4 Procedural Knowledge Learning (chunking and EBBS)
finding: The current manual lists the known causes of incorrect or over-general learned rules, which is the practical form of the correctness checklist from Assanie 2022. Learning is off by default. A rule is built the moment a result reaches the parent state, before the impasse is resolved.
numbers: No numbers. Listed risks: over-general justifications; rule repair that is too specific; operator selection knowledge not tracked by default; random, numeric or reinforcement-learned operator choice (EBBS refuses to add the rule); collapsed local negations; results that depend only on a substate no-change impasse (EBBS learns a condition-free rule and rejects it); several rules firing in a substate collapsed into one result; recalled semantic or episodic knowledge that can change later or is opaque; instruction recall.
quote: Chunking is intended to produce the most general rule that is also correct.
limits: First 100,000 of 140,700 characters read. This is the manual, not the thesis; the thesis' 12-issue taxonomy and its 14 agents / 8 domains evaluation were not read.
agent_relevance: Gives a concrete wrong-reuse checklist for gap 2 and 6. Maps to library rules: do not store entries whose result depended on random choice, on a recalled fact that may change, or on an impasse alone; store the preferences that made the choice.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Tested four memory-addition rules (add all, coarse automatic filter, strict human-grade filter, fixed memory) on four agents (RegAgent, EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT). Agents copy retrieved records when the new input is similar (experience-following). Errors stored from earlier runs raise later errors. Strict selection stays close to an error-free memory; add-all and coarse filters widen the gap over time.
numbers: Add-all and coarse selection widen the gap to an error-free-memory variant as the run continues. With strict selection, AgentDriver slowly closes the gap and passes the error-free variant after about 2000 executions. Exact table cells were garbled in text extraction and are not cited.
quote: inclusion of erroneous memory records ... remains inevitable in many cases, even under human inspection
limits: Tasks are regression and driving-style tasks plus a synthetic agent, not reasoning chains. Gate quality, not trigger, was varied. Simple one-shot demonstrations as memory.
agent_relevance: Most direct measurement of ungated versus gated library at one budget. Supports gap 1 for the gate half: gate strength matters and a weak gate (coarse LLM judge) can be as bad as none. Trigger half still untested.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) memory deletion and misaligned experience replay
finding: Demotion by use: delete a record after at least n retrievals if its mean downstream utility is below a threshold. This beat age-based deletion when the utility judge was good (strict), and hurt when the judge was coarse. Records that passed the entry check but led to worse later outputs were found and removed. Period-based deletion shrinks memory a lot with small loss; the combined rule gives the best size/performance balance.
numbers: Fixed-size memory test: 100 records for EHRAgent and 180 for AgentDriver; managed memory beat a fixed memory. Retained records had lower error than deleted ones (KDE plot). Under a task shift, history-based deletion did worse than combined deletion on EHRAgent. Table 2 cell values were interleaved in extraction and are not cited.
limits: Four agents, authors' evaluators, GPT-4o-mini family. Utility judge quality decided whether deletion helped or hurt.
agent_relevance: Closes gap 9 in part: a match-then-fail demotion rule has a measured design (retrieval count n plus mean utility), and it only works with a reliable judge. Our code check is a strict judge, so the favorable case applies.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Distilled strategies from both successes and failures (LLM-judge labelled) beat no memory, raw trajectory memory (Synapse) and workflow memory (AWM) on WebArena. AWM fell below no-memory for Claude-3.7-sonnet.
numbers: WebArena overall success rate and steps. Gemini-2.5-flash: no memory 40.5 (9.7 steps), Synapse 42.1, AWM 44.1, ReasoningBank 48.8 (8.3 steps), with parallel/sequential scaling 51.8. Gemini-2.5-pro: 46.7, 47.7, 47.6, 53.9, 56.3. Claude-3.7-sonnet: 41.7, 42.6, 40.8 (AWM, below no memory), 46.3.
limits: Judge labels success without ground truth; authors' own method; one benchmark family (WebArena, plus Mind2Web and SWE-bench). Abstract says up to 20% relative gain, 16% fewer steps.
agent_relevance: Distilled rule beating raw case here (Synapse) is the opposite of Wang et al. 2026 (K15), so gap 5 stays unresolved and depends on how the distillation is judged. Also shows an unfiltered workflow library can drop under baseline.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank, failure-trajectory ablation and scaling analysis
finding: Adding failure trajectories helped ReasoningBank but barely moved baselines, which store only successes. Extra rollouts (test-time scaling) helped strong memory and did little for weak memory.
numbers: Success-only to success+failure: Synapse 40.6 to 41.7; ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7 (WebArena, Gemini-2.5-flash). Scaling raised Synapse only 40.6 to 41.2 and AWM 44.4 to 45.5.
limits: Ablation on a subset of WebArena; failure labels from an LLM judge, which can be wrong.
agent_relevance: Impasses are failures. This is evidence that storing the lesson from a failed attempt is worth more than storing only successes, but only when the lesson is distilled rather than copied.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory (EACL 2026)
finding: A model-curated notebook of strategies and code snippets, rewritten after each query, lifts reasoning accuracy. Curated memory beat appending every past query and answer. This is a reasoning task test of an after-every-query library, with no impasse trigger.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 23.3 to 50.0 (cumulative DC-Cu); AIME 2025 6.7 to 36.7; GPQA-Diamond 59.6 to 68.7 (retrieval-synthesis DC-RS; retrieval alone 63.6). GPT-4o Game of 24 10 to 99 (DC-RS). Full-history append: Sonnet 26.7 on AIME 2024; GPT-4o fell from 20.0 to 6.7. Majority vote of 3 gave no gain (23.3 on AIME 2024, 6.7 on 2025). GPT-4o on GPQA only 57.1 to 58.1.
limits: AIME sets are 30 questions each, so one question is 3.3 points. Small models (GPT-4o-mini, Haiku) gained little or fell. Several runs in a fixed question order.
agent_relevance: The nearest reasoning-task evidence for a library. Shows that uncurated accumulation can fall far below baseline and that curation matters, but still no comparison with an impasse trigger. Part-answer to gap 1.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet, discussion of retrieval noise and error clusters
finding: Authors report that bad heuristics in memory get reused on neighbouring queries and are amplified, retrieval of weak examples caused dips, and rewrites sometimes truncated memory ('previous content preserved').
numbers: No separate rate given. Example: GPT-4o on GPQA gained only 1 point under retrieval. Qualitative analysis of outputs and memory.
quote: faulty heuristics that slip into memory can be equally amplified
agent_relevance: Gap 2 is still unmeasured: the field reports the effect in words but no one has counted false reuse on near-duplicate tasks needing different fixes.

source: Wang et al. (2023) LEGO-Prover: Neural Theorem Proving with Growing Libraries
finding: A growing library of lemmas that Isabelle has already verified, in a reasoning task (formal proofs). Removing the library (and the lemma evolver) lowers the pass rate, and the gap widens as the library fills.
numbers: miniF2F-valid, 50 attempts per problem: 50.4% with growing library vs 47.1% without (+3.3 points). The advantage is initially minimal and widens as the library expands (Fig 3a). Main results with human informal proofs: +7.3 points valid and +4.5 test over Subgoal-Learning; model-written informal proofs 52.4% valid and 45.5% test.
limits: Ablation only at 50 attempts due to cost, one run, validation set. Library is filled by verified lemmas (gated), no ungated comparison. Search summaries disagreed on the figure (4.9 points in the ICLR text); the arXiv text read gives 3.3.
agent_relevance: A reasoning-task library with a hard gate (the proof checker). Gain is real but small (3.3 points) and shows a growth curve shape: little early, more later.

source: Wang, Gandhi, Neubig, Fried (2025) Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks (ASI), COLM 2025
finding: Direct ablation of the verification gate: same induction, with or without an execution check, and in memory versus in the action space. Gated induction beats ungated induction.
numbers: WebArena shopping site success rate: unverified text skills in memory 32.6; verified program skills in memory 36.4; verified text 39.0; verified program as actions 40.1 (ASI). Text says verification alone gives +4.2 while the table gives +3.8. Overall: adaptive agents +11.0 to +23.5 over static; ASI +11.3 over AWM; 10.6% to 15.3% fewer steps.
limits: One site (shopping) for the ablation; format and verification were changed together in the first step, so the clean gate effect is the 3.8-4.2 points. Authors' own method.
agent_relevance: Best single test of the gate half of gap 1: about +4 points at the same induction budget. It does not vary the trigger.

source: Wang et al. (2025) ASI, induction pass rates
finding: A strict gate admits few entries. ASI's programs passed verification on 15.6% of turns while AWM, with no execution check, added a skill on 31.4% of turns.
numbers: 15.6% vs 31.4% of turns; 70 correct episodes for AWM and 58 for ASI used for induction.
agent_relevance: Gate cuts library growth in half. Planning number: expect only 15-30% of attempted compilations to survive a code check, so the cost of attempts matters.

source: CogRec: Soar plus LLM recommender, ablation and learning convergence (full text re-read)
finding: The text defines three ablations (no LLM bootstrap, no chunking, no Soar) and says: without chunking the model-call frequency stays high; with chunking it falls and settles on a low stable plateau. Without bootstrap performance drops sharply; without chunking it falls toward the LLM-only baseline.
numbers: Figure 4 gives call frequency against interaction steps; no tabulated values were recoverable from the text layer (the plot axes were encoded text). ML-1M HR@10 0.3124 vs 0.2956 for Soar alone as in the critique.
limits: Recommender, not reasoning. Plateau point not stated numerically. No replication.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly answered qualitatively: the ablation exists and the plateau is in the figure; the number of tasks to plateau and the frozen-scaffold case stay unmeasured.

source: Kadu and Krishnan (2026) Within-Episode Failure Recovery in LLM Agents via Progress-Gated Dual-Process Routing (ICML 2026 workshop)
finding: A stuck trigger in an LLM agent: a slow causal-diagnosis step fires only after 5 consecutive low-progress scores, while a fast refinement step runs every 3 steps. Slow activation outputs a trigger, a diagnostic and a verified fix.
numbers: ALFWorld 134 tasks, 10 seeds, no demos. Qwen-3-8B 35.1 to 75.4; GPT-5 46.3 to 88.1. Versus compute-matched 1-shot LATS +2.7 points (p about 0.01); versus Tree of Thoughts +5.7; versus Self-Refine +6.7.
limits: Event page only (abstract and summary). The gate-versus-fixed-schedule ablation was not on the page, and the paper itself (OpenReview) was not opened. Workshop paper.
agent_relevance: This is the closest published thing to an impasse trigger with a numeric threshold (5 low-progress steps). Gap 4 is not answered: no typed-versus-generic ablation, and the trigger ablation is not shown.

source: Heathcote, Brown, Mewhort (2000) The power law repealed; Evans, Brown, Mewhort, Heathcote (2018) Refining the law of practice, Psychological Review 125(4):592-605
finding: Search-result summaries only (full text blocked, 403). The 2018 paper proposes a delayed exponential law (slow-fast-slow) with power and exponential as limits, and reports a clear majority of paradigms favouring the delayed exponential. The 2000 paper used 40 data sets, 7,910 series, 475 subjects, 24 experiments and found exponential better for all unaveraged sets, with averaging biasing toward power.
numbers: Per the summary only; no counts for the 2018 paper.
limits: Not opened. Human practice data, not library gain curves.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: no LLM library study fits a functional form. Voyager (d01), LEGO-Prover (d11) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (d09) show an early-flat-then-rising shape, consistent with the delayed form, but none fitted a curve.

source: Assanie (2022) Learning General and Correct Procedural Knowledge in a Cognitive Architecture, PhD thesis, University of Michigan
finding: Could not open the thesis PDF: the repository returned 403 or a bot page and the file link 404. From the repository record seen in search: four necessary conditions for correct behaviour summarisation, a taxonomy of correctness problems by those conditions, and EBBS that fixes or detects 12 issues. The practical issue list is in the Soar manual (d04), which was read.
numbers: Abstract-level only (12 issues, four conditions). The 14 agents / 8 domains figure is not confirmed here.
limits: Unopened primary. Gap 6 stays partly open.
agent_relevance: Use the Soar manual list (d04) as the working checklist; do not cite thesis numbers.

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to the Soar Cognitive Architecture, arXiv 2205.03854
finding: Seen via search summary only in this pass. States that chunking was reimplemented as EBBS and that chunking needs deterministic substate decisions, so it is not used when decisions depend on numeric preferences.
limits: Search snippet, not read this pass (a text copy exists in the scratch folder from an earlier pass; its content was not rechecked here).
agent_relevance: Supports K06: a compiled entry is only safe when the substate step is repeatable. For an LLM sampling step, require a code check or repeat run before compiling.
